reviewer: Independent reviewer (Claude Opus 5 CLI documentation review seat)

fixture.providerMode: dedicated local OpenID Connect fixture; full browser authorization and callback; no external identity-provider account

steps.action: Set up later on the final invitation step ends onboarding and cannot be reopened
steps.actual: On Invite your team both Finish and Set up later were present. Set up later ended onboarding and entered the app, the onboarding record flipped to completed true, and a later visit to /welcome redirected to Home, so the wizard cannot be reopened. Completion is instance-wide and irreversible, so Finish and the Welcome-step Set up later could not also be exercised here.

steps.action: Organization name saves on Enter, restores on Escape, and survives a reload
steps.actual: The name field started as "". Typing Helix Legal Group and pressing Enter showed the Saved status and survived a reload. Typing Discarded Draft Name then pressing Escape restored Helix Legal Group, and a reload confirmed the discarded text was never saved.

steps.action: Default locale offers only English (United States) and the default timezone saves
steps.actual: Default locale exposed exactly one option, English (United States), matching the guide. Default timezone is a searchable combobox that started at UTC; choosing its option, labelled "Europe/London (GMT+01:00)", showed Saved and held after a reload.

steps.action: Logo upload accepts a supported image and rejects an unsupported file
steps.actual: A one-pixel PNG set through the Upload control beside Logo reported Saved. A text/plain file was refused with the field error, so the guide instruction to correct format or size and retry matches the behavior.

steps.action: The activated colleague is Active and can sign in with the password set from the invitation
steps.actual: After following her emailed invitation and choosing a password, Priya Raman shows as Active with role Legal team member. She signed in with that password in a separate browser context, and Settings then Users offered her no Invite user control, so the role limits organisation administration as the guide says.

steps.action: Re-inviting a pending address with the same role resends instead of adding a duplicate row
steps.actual: Inviting tomas.novak@helix.example a second time as Contributor, the same role, sent a further set-password email and left exactly one user row. This is the same-role resend the corrected guide describes.

steps.action: Re-inviting the same pending address with a different role is refused, not resent
steps.actual: Inviting the same pending address as Legal team member instead of Contributor was refused with "This user already exists with a different role." No further email was sent and no second row appeared, so only a same-role re-invite resends. The corrected guide now states this refusal.

steps.action: An invitation for an already activated account is refused
steps.actual: Inviting Priya Raman again after activation was refused with "This user has already activated their account." and produced no email, matching the guide statement that invitations for already activated accounts are rejected.

steps.action: Resend invite and Revoke invite act on the pending rows
steps.actual: Resend invite delivered a replacement link for a row whose original invitation was created while outbound email was unavailable, so a failed delivery still leaves a recoverable pending row. Revoke invite then removed both unused invitations from the list. These row actions are icon buttons whose accessible names are "Resend the invite to <address>" and "Revoke the invite to <address>".
